map.人员安全疏散时间估算（流量法） 使用指南: Personnel safe-evacuation time estimation (flow method) user guide
map.人员安全疏散时间估算器（流量法）。输入人员密度、出口宽度与流量系数，按流量法估算: Personnel safe-evacuation time estimator (flow method). Input personnel density, exit width and flow coefficient; estimates total evacuation time by the flow method, for building fire evacuation design and safety assessment.
map.将行走时间、出口排队时间和预动作时间相加，估算人员完成疏散所需时间。: Sum walking time, exit queuing time and pre-action time to estimate the time for personnel to complete evacuation.
map.疏散设计中，由人数、出口宽度、人流速度与行走距离估算总疏散时间。: In evacuation design, estimate total evacuation time from population, exit width, pedestrian speed and walking distance.
map.预案编制时，把行走时间、出口排队时间与预动作时间叠加得到总耗时。: When drafting a plan, stack walking time, exit queuing time and pre-action time to get total duration.
map.出口能力不足会形成排队瓶颈，是疏散时间的主要来源。: Insufficient exit capacity forms a queuing bottleneck and is the main source of evacuation time.
map.算例：100 人、出口宽 2m、流量 1.5 人/(s·m)、距离 30m、速度: Example: 100 people, exit width 2m, flow 1.5 persons/(s*m), distance 30m, speed 1.2m/s, pre-action 30s
map.：行走 = 30/1.2 = 25.0 s；排队 = 100/(2×1.5) =: : walking = 30/1.2 = 25.0 s; queuing = 100/(2 x 1.5) = 33.3 s; total evacuation = 25.0 + 33.3 + 30 = 88.3 s (approx 1.47 min); exit capacity = 2 x 1.5 = 3.00 persons/s.
map.：总时间 = 行走 + 排队 + 预动作，其中『排队 = 人数/(出口宽×单位宽: : total time = walking + queuing + pre-action, where "queuing = count / (exit width x unit-width flow)" is most sensitive to the result. Widening exits or diversion can significantly reduce queuing time.
map.单位宽度人流流量取多少？: What unit-width pedestrian flow is used?
map.常见设计取值约 1.3–1.5 人/(s·m)（水平出口），楼梯略低。实际受人员: Common design values about 1.3-1.5 persons/(s*m) (horizontal exit), slightly lower for stairs. Affected by crowd composition and familiarity; this tool uses input, and values should refer to current evacuation design codes.
map.指人员发现火情到开始撤离的反应时间（察觉、判断、广播、起身），通常 30–60: Reaction time from fire detection to starting evacuation (notice, judge, broadcast, stand up), typically 30-60 s. It does not depend on exit capacity but occupies a large share of total evacuation time, and drills can significantly shorten it.
